basis: Reported syndrome combines craniofacial and hand malformations/contractures with congenital septal and pulmonary-valve defects; frequencies are unspecified.
Gonadal dysgenesis causes impaired endocrine gonadal development and sex differentiation; gonadal tumors occur in a minority.
Thanatophoric type 2 skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia with severe respiratory impairment occurs in most patients due to the markedly restricted thorax.
Spastic ataxia affects central and peripheral nerves; hypodontia occurs in 80-99%. Nystagmus is neurologic; reduced visual acuity occurs in only 1/7.
Structural skeletal myopathy with nemaline rods; respiratory weakness reflects affected skeletal muscles rather than intrinsic lung disease.
Viral hemorrhagic disease with common blood-cell abnormalities and bleeding; vascular dysfunction with capillary leak occurs in 80-99%. Hepatic and renal abnormalities are occasional.
Inherited neuroendocrine neoplasm arising in the small intestine; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-organ disease.
Benign tumor arising from thyroid follicular cells; the thyroid is an endocrine gland.
Inherited motor and sensory peripheral nerve disorders; optic atrophy, retinal disease and metabolic abnormalities are restricted to particular subtypes.
Immune-mediated granulomatous orofacial inflammation and facial neuropathy define the syndrome; inflammatory skin abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Disorder located in synovial tissue of the musculoskeletal system; immune mechanisms do not apply to every subtype.
Malignant tumor originating in the CNS; weakness and impaired mobility reflect neurologic injury rather than direct muscle or joint disease.
Red-cell aplasia; intellectual disability 4/6, brachydactyly 4/6 and pes planus 3/6; aortic regurgitation 1/3 meets threshold but evidence is limited. Obesity is separately coded.
Purine-synthesis enzyme deficiency whose defining spectrum includes peripheral neuropathy and sensorineural hearing loss; optic atrophy varies by phenotype.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and axonal neuropathy define the disorder; structural kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/9. Respiratory distress occurs in only 1/9.
Pure psychiatric mood disorder without defining damage to any of the 13 organ axes.
Fibrotic thickening of the pericardium restricts cardiac filling; the umbrella diagnosis does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Degeneration of intervertebral discs; nerve compression is not established as common direct injury across the umbrella diagnosis.
Mycobacterial infection of the skin; pulmonary involvement is not required or established as common for this cutaneous disease.
Childhood hypothyroidism with defining hypothyroid myopathy and muscular pseudohypertrophy.
Age-related outward turning of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Syndromic forms represented here share pectoral muscle or chest-wall/limb malformations, especially Poland syndrome. Breast hypoplasia itself has no axis; renal defects are subtype-specific.
ADCY5-related neurologic movement disorder; hypotonia and dyskinesia do not establish intrinsic muscle disease. Cardiomyopathy and heart failure occur in 5-29%.
Inherited impairment of fatty-acid energy metabolism; hepatic, cardiac, muscle and neurologic injury vary substantially across subtypes and are not established across this umbrella.
Congenital spinal cord splitting with a defining incomplete osseous spur; both neural and vertebral skeletal malformation are intrinsic to this subtype.
